purpose: Evaluate record-scoped context/detail extraction on short real public HTML fragments beyond media listings.
protocol: Family assignments were declared before annotation, inference or model outputs. Facts were manually selected by inspecting source DOM; heldout families must not enter fitting, synthetic augmentation or threshold selection. A second development-only expansion assigned sqlite.org, loc.gov, usa.gov and mit.edu before capture; loc.gov failed. The original validation and heldout labels were not changed.

collection.policy: One listing and robots.txt per family, plus budgeted same-family redirects; robots-aware, minimum 2-second host interval. No linked content pages, browser rendering or third-party APIs requested. LionDine capture was shared from the parent task without a second request.

capture_failures.error: The source requires Cloudflare browser verification (HTTP 403). Trackify could not read its listing. Use an accessible feed or import a CSV; saved entries were kept.

collection.raw_storage: Full captures remain ignored under backend/data/context-expansion/raw. Source SHA256 refers to the saved UTF-8 capture, not compressed HTTP wire bytes.

annotation_contract.selector: Unique CSS selector for the exact anchor inside html, independent of URL normalization.
annotation_contract.boundary_selector: Manually identified record container. Nested contextual links can belong to one target record. GNU controls intentionally use the anchor itself.
annotation_contract.required: Case/whitespace normalized source phrases that must be present in the extracted details. LionDine includes every food label in its retained open hall.
annotation_contract.forbidden: Distinctive source facts from adjacent records; must not be copied into this record.
annotation_contract.title: Visible source anchor text, including original icon text if present.
annotation_contract.fragment_sha256: Hash of the committed html string encoded in UTF-8.
annotation_contract.provenance: Real-source excerpt; neutral outer wrapper and removal of scripts/styles/SVG/comments are disclosed. No model-generated labels.

efficient_expansion: Capture a listing once and annotate its record boundary plus required/forbidden facts once, then reuse that HTML for all candidate models.
Derive positive/negative boundary candidates offline from those labels, keeping all candidates from a family in the same split.

Apply bounded layout transformations only to development records: extra neutral wrappers, sibling order where semantic association remains unchanged, harmless whitespace and class changes, repeated neighbor controls.
Inherit source family, split, parent example id and transformation seed on every synthetic variant; reject duplicates by normalized fragment checksum.
Keep required facts and forbidden neighbor facts fixed during layout mutations, and validate their DOM association before using variants.
Report real-family results separately from synthetic robustness results. Synthetic row counts are not evidence of wider real-site coverage.
limitations: Eleven source families and 33 anchors are a small targeted diagnostic suite, not an unbiased estimate of web-wide accuracy.
Each fragment retains two or three neighboring records. It does not test full-page discovery, link classification, pagination, scripts, redirects or network-access failures.

Eleven of twelve selected source families were captured. Library of Congress returned Cloudflare HTTP 403 and was excluded without bypassing it. Accessibility here is not a promise that another location or date will succeed.
Public site content is volatile. Captured dates and menu/status facts describe the saved snapshot only.

New heldout context tasks may share domains with older unrelated link-classification datasets; this is task-level heldout context evidence, not a claim the production model has never seen these domains.
Source snippets are retained for regression/evaluation with attribution; no grant of source-content licensing is implied.
No automatic boundary labels came from the currently deployed record model, avoiding self-confirming evaluation.
